title: Over-Limit Restoration on Past-Due Northgate Card Accounts
content:
Bringing a past-due **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** account back to good standing includes an over-limit restoration, which follows the amount owed today less the amounts still under dispute:

- where that amount is above the credit limit, the over-limit restoration is the excess;
- where it is within the credit limit but leaves less room than the tier's minimum payment floor (30.00 USD on the Northgate Secured Card, 40.00 USD on every other card), it is that floor less the room left;
- in every other case there is none.

**The amount owed today** is read from the account history: purchases and cash advances, interest, fees, returned payments, re-billed dispute credits and credit balance refunds raise it; payments, merchant credits, dispute credits, fee reversals and reward credits lower it; the amounts still under dispute are the disputed amounts of the disputes opened on the account less the amounts that have left dispute status. The room left is the credit limit less the amount owed today net of the amounts still under dispute.

| Amount owed today less the amounts under dispute, against a 1000.00 limit and a 40.00 floor (hypothetical) | Room left | Over-limit restoration |
|---|---|---|
| 1035.00 | none — 35.00 over | 35.00 |
| 1000.00 | 0.00 | 40.00 |
| 975.00 | 25.00 | 15.00 |
| 960.00 | 40.00 | none |
| 700.00 | 300.00 | none |

**Hypothetical history.** Purchases of 1200.00, interest of 20.00 and a late fee of 32.00 raise the amount owed; payments of 300.00 lower it; a dispute of 60.00 is still open. The amount owed today is 952.00 and, net of the 60.00 under dispute, 892.00; against a 900.00 limit on a 40.00-floor card the room left is 8.00, so the over-limit restoration is 32.00.
